# cockpit

> cockpit is the local environment coding agents work from on a product of one or many repositories. One reviewed `cockpit.toml` gives Claude Code, Codex CLI and OpenCode the same instructions, skills, permissions and guard hook, including every repository's guides and directory access (`cockpit sync` writes them, `cockpit check` fails on drift). `cockpit session` runs the product's own Compose stack on the live checkouts with a leased port family per checkout, worktrees included (`cockpit use` serves a sibling from one, `cockpit stacks prune` cleans up after a deleted one), and starts the agent inside it; `ps`, `restart`, `rebuild` and `exec` act on one service, `--profile` adds Compose profiles, and `cockpit pull` fast-forwards every checkout. Work orders (objective, scope, criteria with checks) are graded the way the cockpit chooses: by default a fresh read-only agent run (another listed tool when one is available, otherwise the same tool in a new run), or the checks alone, or the agent's own report; the record names which. A failed check fails the grade in every mode; where a model grades, it also judges changes outside scope, flagged test changes and the agent's amendments to the contract. Work orders record their lasting decisions as decision records (`work note --decision`, `work decide`), and `cockpit docs check` reports documents that cite removed paths. `cockpit browser drive` reports each route's console errors and failed requests as evidence (`--fail-on-findings` makes them fail). An agent may sync its own `cockpit.toml` edit when it does not widen what agents may do. The instructions and guard need only Git and Node.js; the stack needs Docker Compose. Not a sandbox. Pre-1.0, macOS and Linux.

## Set cockpit up

- [Getting started](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/b0dea/cockpit/main/docs/getting-started.md): the on-ramp, the safety contract and exact non-interactive commands for an agent setting cockpit up, and the bring-up sequence
- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/b0dea/cockpit/main/README.md): what cockpit is, a sample `cockpit.toml`, the quickstart with its requirements and caveats

## Reference

- [CLI reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/b0dea/cockpit/main/docs/cli-reference.md): every command, flag, exit code and diagnostic
- [Configuration essentials](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/b0dea/cockpit/main/docs/configuration-essentials.md): the `cockpit.toml` tables a typical cockpit sets, with minimal snippets
- [Configuration reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/b0dea/cockpit/main/docs/configuration-reference.md): every `cockpit.toml` field with its type, default and constraints, and a link to the JSON Schema
- [Concepts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/b0dea/cockpit/main/docs/concepts.md): the terms the commands and diagnostics use
